etymology_text:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek Μοῦσα (Moûsa)
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Hellenic *-kos
Ancient Greek -κός (-kós)
Ancient Greek -ικός (-ikós)
Ancient Greek μουσικός (mousikós)
Ancient Greek μουσική (mousikḗ)bor.
Latin mūsicalbor.
Spanish música
Learned borrowing from Latin mūsica, from Ancient Greek μουσική (τέχνη) (mousikḗ (tékhnē), “(art) of the Muses”). Compare the doublet murga, which probably resulted from a semi-popular form of the word.
